_about: Settings for npm run models. 'defaults' apply to every model; a model's own entry (keyed by its file name in models-src/) overrides them. Each entry's 'changes' is the record of what we altered, which CC BY asks us to state.

defaults._textureSize: Longest side in pixels, per texture slot. Colour and normal carry the fabric detail; roughness, metalness and occlusion read the same at half size.

National Costume.glb._place: The scan arrives in arbitrary units, facing -Z and floating off-centre. Height and lift are estimates for an adult wearer of about 1.70 m: collar near 1.47 m, the breeches' knee bands and the cape hem near 0.40 m. Adjust by eye.
National Costume.glb._textureSize: A scan has one colour texture and no normal or roughness maps, so it can afford 4K and still sit inside the GPU budget.
National Costume.glb.changes: A hole in the cape's white lining patched with a new piece of lining in Blender (scripts/blender/patch-national-lining.py): a thin surface fitted over the hole, its stripes continued from the lining around it in a small texture of its own. Turned 180° to face the front, scaled to an estimated real height and centred on the turntable. Stray atlas UVs clamped to 0–1. Simplified from 500k to ~117k triangles (meshoptimizer). The 4K colour texture converted to WebP. Geometry compressed with meshopt. This optimised model is shared under CC BY-SA 4.0, as the original licence requires.
National Costume.glb._clampUVs: 47 of 134,629 atlas UVs strayed up to 0.4% outside 0–1, which kept all UVs as 32-bit floats.
National Costume.glb._source: models-src/National Costume.glb is the patched scan, written by the Blender script from the original in models-src/originals/.
National Costume.glb._simplify: 0.23 (was 0.25): Blender's re-export and the patch added ~0.15 MB, and 0.23 brings the file back under the 3 MB budget (2.98 MB, 117k triangles) with no visible loss in the push-ins.

Parade Armour.glb._place: A full suit, helmet to sabatons, already in metres (1.67 m) with its feet at the bottom. Its front faces +X, so it is turned -90°. No lift: it stands on the plinth.
Parade Armour.glb._texture: The 4K download (a 4096 PNG), converted to WebP. In a push-in the etched scrollwork and the figures in the breastplate's medallions are crisp at 4K and soft at 1K. It costs ~2 MB of file and fits the GPU budget (~89 MB).
Parade Armour.glb.changes: Turned -90° to face the front and centred on the turntable. Simplified from 1M to ~450k triangles (meshoptimizer). Colour texture converted to WebP. Geometry compressed with meshopt.
Parade Armour.glb._simplify: Steel scans carry their relief (repoussé lions, scrollwork, rivets) in the geometry, not the texture. At 150k triangles the relief collapsed into faceted 'foil'; 300k still lost it; 450k keeps most of it. The geometry is ~4.3 MB of the 6.55 MB file (1K texture: 4.53 MB, 2K: 5.02 MB, 4K: 6.55 MB), so only a normal map baked from the 1M original onto a ~150k mesh brings it near the 3 MB budget.

Calligraphy Dress.glb._place: An Artec Leo scan in millimetres, already facing front. Height 1.42 m is its true size, shoulder to hem; the hem sits 5 cm above the plinth, as on an invisible dress form. The scan leaned about 6° back and 2.5° sideways (the chest 12 cm behind and 5 cm beside the hem's centre), so tilt stands it upright; after it, every cross-section from hem to chest is centred within 1 cm. The forearms are bent forward from the scan, so the axis is centred on the skirt (centreOn 0.25), not the whole bounds; that also keeps the hotspots in place if the sleeves are re-posed.
Calligraphy Dress.glb.changes: Stood upright (tilted 5.5° forward and 2.4° sideways), scaled from millimetres to metres and centred on the turntable under the skirt. Simplified from 463k to ~116k triangles (meshoptimizer). The 4K colour texture converted to WebP. Geometry compressed with meshopt.
